newsitem.title: BRAZIL: New Brazil coffee council to be set up Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: New Brazil coffee council to be set up Tuesday.

text.p: Brazil will set up a new coffee policy-making council on Tuesday next week, the official coordinating interministerial negotiations said.
Wilson Calvo Mendes de Araujo of the Presidential Chief of Staff told Reuters a ceremony had been scheduled for 1200 local/1400 GMT in the Presidential Palace.
He added that the number of members the Deliberative Council for Coffee Policy (CDPC) will have had not yet been resolved.
"The question of how many members it will have is the only outstanding issue," Araujo said. He said he was waiting for a final response from the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.
According to the original proposal, which came from a parliamentary committee, the CDPC was to have up to 20 members, divided between the private and public sectors.
Its function will be to determine future coffee policy, which the private sector claims has lacked focus recently.
Early this month, the government published a decree allowing the council to be set up under the auspices of the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.
